trust_decision.summary: At the pinned commit nothing decides who may talk to the dashboard: the Flask app serves every request that reaches the loopback port, and isolation rests only on the default 127.0.0.1 bind, which DNS rebinding defeats; the fix decides per request from the Host header at the server start of the dashboard app.

landing_point.why: SerenaDashboardAPI.run is the only place the dashboard's Flask server is started, so a reader of the advisory ('unauthenticated Flask dashboard on a fixed port') looks there for the missing request-level authorisation.

fix_sites.entry_point: SerenaDashboardAPI.run(host, port) public API, called through run_in_thread (src/serena/dashboard.py:782-787) from SerenaAgent.__init__ (src/serena/agent.py:666-668), i.e. the `serena start-mcp-server` CLI command (src/serena/cli.py:227)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/serena/dashboard.py:945-995 (SerenaDashboardTrayManager: Flask app created at 945, /health /register /update_project /unregister at 950-995, served at 1144)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the dashboard, so the tray manager (experimental tray-UI helper, documented as tested on Windows only) and the project server (a separate, explicitly started service that only runs read-only tools) read as neighbouring features rather than part of this advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate access from outside the loopback interface, which the project itself ships: the image rewrites web_dashboard_listen_address to 0.0.0.0 (Dockerfile:67, DOCKER.md:31) and compose publishes the dashboard as host port 8080 -> container 24282 (compose.yaml:14). A fix that matches only '127.0.0.1:{port}'/'localhost:{port}' rejects every legitimate request in that setup (Host is 'localhost:8080' or a LAN address while the bind port is 24282), and DashboardManager already rewrites 0.0.0.0 to localhost for the viewer URL (src/serena/agent.py:419-422). The allowed set must come from the configured bind address, not from a literal pair.

O6_input_shapes: every other shape is rejected, including `127.0.0.1` without an explicit port, `[::1]:<port>`, case variants of localhost, and a forwarded port that differs from the bind port

O7_producer.where: src/serena/config/serena_config.py:722 (web_dashboard_listen_address, default rewritten to 0.0.0.0 by Dockerfile:67 and normalised to localhost for the viewer URL at src/serena/agent.py:419-422)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The whole tray-manager Flask app accepts any Host; POST /register with open_viewer=true makes the manager open an attacker-supplied dashboard_url in the user's browser (and /update_project, /unregister mutate its instance table)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: separate helper component of the tray UI, experimental and documented as tested on Windows only, not the dashboard the advisory names
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 165 lines below the fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Project server POST /query_project executes any read-only Serena tool (file contents, memories, configuration) over unauthenticated HTTP on the fixed port 0x5EA1
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: documented as a separate service (docs/02-usage/070_security.md:44) that is started only explicitly and is limited to read-only tools

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a tray-manager route that opens or spawns a viewer for a caller-supplied URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the class already opens dashboards from data posted to /register (open_viewer at 970-971), so an explicit '/open' or '/open_dashboard' endpoint taking a url is a natural extension

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a write-capable sibling of /query_project reusing the same tool dispatch without the is_readonly gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _query_project already dispatches any tool by name (95-98); dropping or bypassing the read-only filter is a one-line change for a maintainer who wants edits over this route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second launcher for the same Flask object (a WSGI/ASGI bootstrap, or gunicorn/waitress under compose.yaml:18) that never registers the check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix attaches the check at launch time inside run() rather than at app creation, so a new serving path silently loses the protection while all tests of run() still pass

O9_family: unauthenticated loopback HTTP service / DNS rebinding (CWE-306, CWE-352)

O10_build.toolchain: uv + hatchling; requires-python >=3.11,<3.15; pytest 8.4.1 + pytest-xdist via `uv run poe test`; Flask 3.1.3 / werkzeug 3.1.7 pinned in pyproject.toml:26,49
O10_build.project_tests: test/serena/test_dashboard.py exists at the pinned commit: it builds SerenaDashboardAPI with a dummy agent and log handler (lines 27-32) and calls helper methods directly; there is no HTTP-level or Host-header test, and the fix diff adds none.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject non-loopback request.remote_addr (a no-op against DNS rebinding, whose traffic does arrive from 127.0.0.1) or add an Origin/Referer check, in the dashboard app only, and call it validated.
